newsitem.title: MEXICO: Mexican shoemaker Moymen plans 1997 IPO.
newsitem.headline: Mexican shoemaker Moymen plans 1997 IPO.

text.p: Mexican shoe manufacturer Moymen is planning to make a public stock offer on the Mexican stock exchange in 1997, company president Carlos Moyano Menchaca said Friday.
"We're consolidating a holding group in which we will place the group's stock, and we plan to enter the mid-size market in the coming year," Moyano told Reuters.
Created in 1983, Moymen has posted strong growth in past years despite shrinking domestic shoe demand since the economic crisis resulting from the peso devaluation in December 1994.
According to Moyano, average shoe production rose to 14,000 pairs per day in 1995 with an emphasis on exports, from 6,000 shoes per day in 1993.
Moymen specializes in medical footwear and exports about 60 percent of its production, largely to the United States, Canada, Puerto Rico, Chile and recently Costa Rica and Panama.
Net sales rose 50 percent in the first nine months of the year to 120 million pesos, compared with the same period in 1995, according to the company.
